exposure: mild gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosed by the International Association of Diabetes and Pregnancy Study Groups (IADPSG) criteria, on no specific treatment
Mild gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosed by IADPSG criteria
cohort: 282 pregnant women with mild GDM defined by one abnormal glucose value at the OGTT according to IADPSG criteria, who did not receive specific treatment for GDM, and 282 pregnant women without GDM, matched for maternal age and pre-gestational BMI. All women were referred to the Instituto Nacional de Perinatología, in Mexico City, for prenatal care and delivery.  Eligibility criteria were singleton pregnancy, age >18 years, gestational age 20-28 weeks, and no history of pre-gestational diabetes. Women with two or more abnormal OGTT values, pre-gestational diabetes, any chronic disease, or multiple pregnancies were excluded.
finding: The risk of APO was similar among Mexican women with mild untreated GDM diagnosed by IADPSG criteria, compared to pregnant women without GDM.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in the rates of cesarean delivery and preterm delivery between women with mild gestational diabetes mellitus and those without.
